errors.text_span: This pie chart illustrates the distribution of categories in which large language models refuse to answer questions.
errors.evidence: The figure contains four separate pie charts, not a single one. The description fails to identify the multi-panel structure of the figure, which is fundamental to its meaning.

errors.text_span: The chart displays a total of six slices, representing six distinct categories: “Safety 1 (1.7%)”, “Safety (9.3%)”, “Misinformation 33 (38.4%)”, “Ethical Advice 14 (16.3%)”, “Lack of Knowledge 5 (83.3%)”, and “Clarification 12 (14.0%)”.
errors.evidence: Because the model misidentified the figure as a single chart, it incorrectly combines slices and values from different charts into a single, non-existent entity. For example, 'Lack of Knowledge 5 (83.3%)' is from the GPT4-o chart, while 'Misinformation 33 (38.4%)' is from the Gemini1.5-Pro chart.
The description lists a value of '1.7%' for the 'Safety' category, but the value shown in the GPT4-o chart is '16.7%'.

The description fails to mention that the figure is composed of four distinct charts, each titled with a different model name (GPT4-o, Gemini1.5-Pro, Llama3.1-70B-Instruct, Llama3.1-405B-Instruct). It does not describe the specific data for each individual model's chart.

errors.text_span: The slices are ordered from largest to smallest in size
errors.evidence: The description claims the slices are ordered by size, but this is not true for any of the individual charts in the figure. For example, in the Gemini1.5-Pro chart, the order appears to be based on the position around the circle, not the size of the slice.
